## Auditor Bot

A configured evaluation: which rules, over which subjects, answerable to whom. Carries `name`, a regime-level `regime`, the `rules`, a `subjectQuery` (a Search Cards filter as JSON), `runsAs`, and `lastRunAt`.

```ts
import { AuditorBot } from '@cardstack/catalog/cards/audit/auditor-bot';
@field bot = linksTo(() => AuditorBot);
```

**It is configuration, not a process.** Nothing here runs on a timer, because the platform has no card-reachable scheduler. A "quarterly review" is a person or an assistant invoking Audit against this card, and `lastRunAt` records that it happened. Naming it a bot and letting it never run itself would be the misleading kind of block; naming it and recording who ran it is honest.

**`runsAs` is not decoration.** A bot never signs off a report: an automated result still needs a name against it, which every certification scheme states and most tools quietly drop. The isolated view says so in words when the field is empty.

`brokenRuleCount` surfaces rules that cannot fire. A rule-set that silently contains three dead rules reports compliance it never tested.

## Example
The linked example is `AuditorBot/supplier-controls`: four ISO 9001 §8.4 supplier controls. Run against two suppliers they produce every status the vocabulary has — pass, fail, unproven and not-applicable — as the linked Audit Results show.

## Non-goals
Does not run, schedule, or write results — Audit does that and stamps `lastRunAt`. Does not hold results or findings. Not a permission: who *may* run it is the SoD check, not this card.
